title: Pico eval notes & ad-hoc rubric (Luisa)
body:
Purpose: quick personal scratch for a tiny, repeatable rubric to triage short regressions and noisy length-bias failures. Not a final doc — playground notes, hypotheses, and quick steps to reproduce.

Context: saw a small but repeatable delta in short-answer quality on v2.3 -> v2.4 (hosted). Delta shows up in 2 token contexts: concise factual Qs and list extraction. Suspect change in sampling temperature default + a KV-cache edge.

Quick rubric (ad-hoc) - apply to a 20-sample mini-batch:
- PASS: >= 80% exact-answer match on short-fact prompts OR 0 critical hallucinations (factual assertions contradicted by provided doc).
- WARN: 50-79% match OR 1 non-critical hallucination (plausible but unverifiable).
- FAIL: <50% match OR >1 critical hallucination OR consistent truncation/premature EOS.
- NOTE: flag length-bias if answers are consistently 4-10 tokens shorter than baseline and relevance score drops >0.15.

Sample prompts used (condensed):
- "What's the launch date for Project X?" (has exact date in doc)
- "List the three compliance controls for dataset ingestion."
- "Summarize in one sentence: <policy-paragraph>"

Observed samples (v2.3 -> v2.4):
- Prompt A: baseline v2.3 -> "2024-09-08"; v2.4 -> "September 2024" (acceptable)
- Prompt B: baseline -> 3-item list; v2.4 -> 2 items (missed control #2) => FAIL pattern for that sample
- Prompt C: short summary baseline -> 18 tokens; v2.4 -> 11 tokens + trailing "..." (sign of EOS/length bias)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Default sampling temperature clamped lower in runtime config for hosted (silent change). Lower temp -> more conservative, shorter outputs in some conds.
2) KV-cache eviction heuristic tightened (for memory saving) causing missing context for list enumeration prompts.
3) Tokenizer boundary change for special unicode leading to token count differences (less likely given other signals).

Quick repro steps (what I ran locally):
- Re-run 20-sample suite on v2.3 (hosted) and v2.4 with exact same seed range and prompt fixtures. Save raw tokens + logits (where available).
- Turn on token-level streaming to capture EOS timestamps.
- Force sampling params to baseline explicit values (temp 0.7, top_p 0.9) on v2.4; if delta closes, hypothesis #1 likely.
- Instrument KV-cache by toggling eviction_threshold to 0.6/0.8/1.0 and see if list completions restore.

Quick metrics to capture per-sample:
- exact_match (boolean), token_length, eos_index, perplexity_est (if logs accessible), human_severity (0/1/2).

Notes to self:
- When filing EVAL-4123, attach raw tokens + a 5-sample small recording of streaming frames. The infra folks will want logs around cache hits/misses.
- Check GH PR 78 for an unrelated runtime change that touched sampling defaults. Might be the culprit.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run small A/B with explicit sampling override in front of traffic (can we stage a quick canary on hosted?): ask operations.
- Get SRE to pull kernel logs for the time window 2026-01-22T02:00 -> 2026-01-22T06:00 where anomaly spike started.
- If KV-cache is root cause, propose conservative rollback or a canary with loosened eviction.

Loose thoughts: short-answer regressions are easy to miss if we only monitor token-level latency and throughput. Add a low-cost heuristic: small periodic 20-sample EM tests on critical prompts per model version after deploy.

Scratch:
- quick bash to fetch hosted logs: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/hosts/v2/requests?model=v2.4&since=2026-01-20 -- save as raw-requests.json
- seed list used: [42, 101, 202, 303, 404] (used in these runs)

End of page. Will turn into a cleaned issue if repro is stable.
